24-032.r: Nominated members: 12 in Rajya Sabha; Lok Sabha's 2 Anglo-Indian seats ended 25 January 2020, so only Rajya Sabha has them; nominated member may be Minister; no vote for President.
24-032.c: When asked (2003) only (c) was right, as the Lok Sabha then had two nominated Anglo-Indians; since 25 January 2020 only the Rajya Sabha has nominated members, so (a) is also true.

24-033.r: Parliament can legislate for the Union of India, the Territory of India, and Indian subjects and their property anywhere in the world.

24-035.r: Parliament may legislate on State List: to implement international agreements (Art 253); by consent of two or more States (Art 252); Rajya Sabha 2/3 resolution (Art 249); during Emergency.

24-038.r: Art 253 → Parliament can make law for whole or any part of India to implement international treaties/agreements, even on State List, without any State's consent.

24-039.r: Residuary subjects (not in State or Concurrent List) → Parliament has exclusive power to legislate (Art 248).

24-040.r: Art 120(1) → Parliament's business in Hindi or English; Speaker/Chairman may let a member who cannot express himself in either speak in his mother tongue.

24-041.r: Yielding the floor → Speaker stops a member and lets another speak; Crossing the floor → changing party; Interpellation → asking Government to explain an act or policy.

24-042.r: Zero Hour (Indian innovation): Lok Sabha 12 noon-1 pm, after Question Hour (11-12); Rajya Sabha 11 am-12 noon; maximum one hour.
24-042.c: Book prints two answers, (c) and (d): Rajya Sabha's Zero Hour is 11 am-12 noon, Lok Sabha's 12 noon-1 pm.

24-046.r: Zero Hour → members raise important matters that cannot be delayed; the book equates it with a question-answer session.

24-047.r: General discussion on a Bill → second reading (first stage of consideration), then clause-by-clause; first reading = introduction; third reading = passing.

24-048.r: Bill at a joint sitting (Art 108(4)) → passed by a simple majority of total members of both Houses present and voting.

24-049.r: If Lok Sabha is dissolved after President notifies a joint sitting, the joint sitting is still held as scheduled (bill does not lapse); a lapsed bill cannot go to one.

24-050.r: Joint sitting → Article 108 (not 109, which covers Money Bills); presided over by the Lok Sabha Speaker.

24-051.r: Joint sitting → Article 108, not 109 (Money Bill procedure); no joint sitting for a Constitution Amendment Bill, which each House passes by special majority (Art 368).

24-052.r: Joint sitting of the two Houses → presided over by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha.

24-053.r: Joint sitting presided by Lok Sabha Speaker (Art 118(4)); if absent → Deputy Speaker → Deputy Chairman of Rajya Sabha → person chosen by members present.
24-053.t: Not the President or Vice-President; the Rajya Sabha Chairman never presides over a joint sitting.

24-057.r: Joint sitting (Art 108): 1st in 1961 (Dowry Prohibition Bill); 2nd in 1978 (Banking Service Commission (Repeal) Bill, 1977); 3rd in March 2002 (POTA).

24-059.r: Joint session (Art 108) → only to pass a Bill on which the two Houses disagree; not for President/VP elections or Constitution amendment; first on Dowry Bill.

24-061.r: Joint sitting: only ordinary bills (not Money or Constitution Amendment bills); Rajya Sabha Deputy Chairman can preside if Speaker and Deputy Speaker absent; quorum 1/10, not 1/6.

24-062.r: Joint sitting (Art 108) → only for ordinary legislation; Money Bill needs none (Rajya Sabha must return it in 14 days); Constitution Amendment passed by each House (Art 368).
24-062.t: Joint sitting is never for Money Bills or Constitution Amendment Bills.

24-065.r: An ordinary legislative Bill → can be introduced in either House of Parliament; a Money Bill only in Lok Sabha.

24-066.r: Lapse on Lok Sabha dissolution (Art 107(5)): bill pending in LS, and LS-passed bill pending in RS; NOT a bill notified for joint sitting (108(5)) or RS bill unpassed by LS (107(4)).

24-067.r: Bills do not lapse on prorogation (Art 107(3)); a bill pending in Rajya Sabha not yet passed by Lok Sabha does not lapse on Lok Sabha's dissolution (Art 107(4)).

24-068.r: No tax levied or collected except by authority of law → Article 265; Art 266 → Consolidated Funds and Public Accounts; Art 300 → suits; Art 368 → amendment.

24-069.r: No one (CAG, Finance Minister or any Minister) can issue money from Consolidated Fund of India (Art 266) without Parliament's authorisation by appropriation (Art 114).

24-070.r: All Union Government revenues, taxes and other receipts → credited to the Consolidated Fund of India (Art 266).
hi: Consolidated Fund of India (भारत की संचित निधि)

24-071.r: Withdrawal of money from the Consolidated Fund of India → must be authorised by Parliament (Art 114).

24-072.r: Charged on Consolidated Fund: President's emoluments; RS Chairman/Deputy and LS Speaker/Deputy salaries; debt charges; SC judges; HC judges' pensions; CAG. Not listed: Election Commission members' salary.

24-073.r: Not charged on Consolidated Fund → Vice-President's salary as VP (Art 112); he is paid as Rajya Sabha Chairman, whose salary is charged.
24-073.t: Chairman of Rajya Sabha's salary is charged; there is no separate charged salary for the Vice-President.

24-074.r: Not charged → Prime Minister's salary; charged (Art 112(3)): President, CJI, HC judges' pensions, CAG, RS Chairman/Deputy, LS Speaker/Deputy; charged items discussed, not voted.

24-075.r: Contingency Fund of India → Article 267; placed at President's disposal for advances to meet unforeseen expenditure.

24-076.r: Contingency Fund (Art 267(1)) → President can advance money for unforeseen expenditure before Parliament's authorisation; no prior approval needed.

24-077.r: Union Budget prepared by Ministry of Finance (not Department of Revenue); Consolidated Fund withdrawal needs Parliament's authorisation (Art 114(3)); Public Account disbursements do not.
24-077.t: Public Account is controlled by the Executive; no Parliament vote needed.

24-078.r: Preparation and presentation of the Union Budget → Department of Economic Affairs (not Department of Revenue or Expenditure).

24-079.r: Annual Financial Statement (Art 112(1)) laid by Finance Minister on behalf of the President, not PM; no demand for grant except on President's recommendation (Art 113(3)).

24-080.r: Demands for Grants (Art 113) → presented to Lok Sabha, usually one per ministry; budget 2025-26 had 102, 2021-22 had 101 → 'none of the above'.

24-081.r: Article 110 → definition of Money Bill; Art 109 → special procedure for Money Bills; Art 111 → assent to Bills.

24-083.r: Money Bill (Art 110): only matters of tax, Government borrowing, custody of Consolidated/Contingency Funds, appropriation, charged expenditure, receipts and audit of Union/State accounts.

24-085.r: NOT a Money Bill matter → imposition of fines or penalties; Money Bill covers taxes, borrowings, custody of Consolidated and Contingency Funds (Art 110).

24-086.r: Wrong: 'Rajya Sabha can detain Finance Bill 14 days' (that is Money Bill) and 'President cannot refuse Finance Bill' (he can return it); Rajya Sabha can amend Finance Bill.

24-087.r: Not correct: 'Money Bill in either House' → only Lok Sabha; Speaker decides if a bill is a Money Bill; Rajya Sabha must return it within 14 days.

24-088.r: Rajya Sabha can amend or reject a Financial Bill (I), but only recommend on a Money Bill within 14 days; joint sitting possible (not necessary) for Financial Bills, never for Money Bills.

24-089.r: Whether a Bill is a Money Bill → decided by the Lok Sabha Speaker; his decision is final (Art 110(3)).

24-090.r: Money Bill certified by Lok Sabha Speaker; his decision is final, not questioned by courts, Parliament or President; endorsed when sent to Rajya Sabha and to President.

24-092.r: Money Bill → presented only in Lok Sabha (Art 109(1)); UPPSC's Hindi paper said 'Finance Bill' but meant Money Bill.

24-093.r: Finance Bill (Art 117(1)) → introduced only in the Lower House (Lok Sabha), on the President's recommendation; never in Council of States.

24-094.r: Money Bill: special procedure Art 109; not introduced in Rajya Sabha; RS may only recommend within fourteen days; Lok Sabha may accept or reject them; deemed passed if not returned.

24-095.r: Money Bill → introduced only in Lok Sabha; Speaker's decision final; no joint session; Rajya Sabha can hold it at most 14 days (Art 109(2)).
